sections.COMMENTS:
Subduction of oceanic crust in the Calabrian Arc began about 80 Ma ago (Faccenna et al., 2001) and is still ongoing along a rather small portion (ca. 150 km) of the arc between the Stretta di Catanzaro (Catanzaro Isthmus) to the north, and the Straits of Messina to the south. The effects of the recent NNW-SSE plate convergence upon subduction gradually decreased with the progressive rotation and south-eastward migration of the Calabrian Arc due to continental collision in Sicily (Cifelli et al., 2008).
The southwestern margin of the subduction interface is characterized by a complex structural setting. Near the Alfeo Seamount, the lateral continuity of the subduction interface is interrupted by a system of NW-SE-trending, high-angle oblique normal faults, NE-side down (Maesano et al., 2020). This fault system consists of a major fault bounding the Alfeo Seamount to the east, and of a more complex en-echelon fault array to the northwest. This system cuts through the entire Ionian crust at least down to the Moho, with increasing displacement from SE to NW, and is interpreted as the Subduction Transform Edge Propagator (STEP, sensu Govers and Wortel, 2005) of the Calabrian subduction zone tentatively identified by Polonia et al. (2011). To the east of the Malta Escarpment, the outer post-Messinian wedge reaches into regions beyond the STEP fault system.
Historical and instrumental earthquake catalogues (ISIDe Working Group, 2007; Guidoboni et al., 2019; Rovida et al., 2021) show a remarkable concentration of damaging earthquakes in the area. In particular, this region has been struck by the 13 December 1990 (Mw 5.6) earthquake; here we can recall that, further to the west, the known destructive 11 January 1693 (Mw 7.3) earthquake has occurred.
The STEP fault system is composed by NW-SE near-vertical faults segments, accommodating the differential motion between the collisional Sicilian orogen and the retreating Calabrian slab with transtensional to strike-slip movements. The STEP fault system unfolded in the Ionian lower plate and it is confined below the accretionary wedge base, which acts as a horizon of mechanical decoupling between the lower and upper plates (Maesano et al., 2020). The dip-slip component of motion of the STEP fault system controls some localized basins in the accretionary wedge of the upper plate. The age of inception of the STEP fault system in the Ionian area is constrained by the development of the basins above the accretionary wedge. Such age is thought to be younger than 2.6 Ma in the Catania offshore, but it becomes progressively younger moving towards the Ionian abyssal plain, where the age of inception is estimated in 1.3 Ma (Maesano et al., 2020). The shallow features associated with the activity of the STEP fault system have been well documented in recent years by different authors using high-resolution geophysical data (Polonia et al., 2011; Gutscher et al., 2016).
